# Choose cloud services from the workload

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `azure-service-selection` · **Azure & Cloud Architecture** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S05-Q018](#S05-Q018)

<p>When would you choose serverless functions for a workload, and what requirement could make that choice unsuitable?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Choose and defend a cloud processing path from workload, data and recipient requirements.</p>

<ul>
<li>Explain when function-based execution fits the work lifecycle.</li>
<li>Choose object or relational storage from concrete access and consistency needs.</li>
<li>Distinguish message recipient topology from worker count.</li>
<li>Trace interrupted processing and define the recovery evidence required.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Start with what the application must do and where its data lives. Execution handles the work, storage holds the resulting state, and messaging connects independent recipients. The questions build that processing path before asking whether a failed step can recover.</p>

<a id="S05-Q018"></a>

### S05-Q018 · Foundation

<p>When would you choose serverless functions for a workload, and what requirement could make that choice unsuitable?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q018](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q018)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q018](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q018)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain when serverless functions are appropriate.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Functions are a managed execution option for application work. Compare the workload’s lifecycle and operating needs rather than treating “serverless” as a universal advantage.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose an execution model from workload constraints and a measurable decision boundary.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify invocation pattern, execution duration, latency needs and state; Azure is a possible context, not a specified service plan. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects the choice to one concrete workload and the constraint it addresses.</li>
<li>Proposes a representative test and explains what result would change the choice.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Equating serverless with no operational work or guaranteed lower cost.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you evaluate the same workload if predictable response latency becomes critical?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q021"></a>

### S05-Q021 · Foundation

<p>Which application workloads fit object or blob storage, and what access requirements would you clarify before choosing it?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q021](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q021)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q021](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q021)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain object/blob storage use cases.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Discuss how the application stores and retrieves objects such as files. Focus on data access and lifecycle rather than reciting product names.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Match a storage model to an application’s data and access patterns.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify object size, access permissions, update behavior and retention; named-service guarantees require separate verification.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects a concrete storage use case to its read and write pattern.</li>
<li>Explains a requirement that could favor another storage model and how to validate it.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Choosing blob storage solely because the data can be serialized as a file.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you test access control and lifecycle behavior for uploaded files?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q022"></a>

### S05-Q022 · Foundation

<p>When would you choose a managed relational database, and which responsibilities would still belong to the application team?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q022](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q022)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q022](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q022)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain managed relational database use cases.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the workload’s relationship, query and consistency needs, then discuss what “managed” means for the operating contract.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Select a database model while retaining clear operational ownership.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a relational business workload; define availability, recovery and access needs without assuming a particular service tier.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects relational requirements to a specific data and query example.</li>
<li>Separates provider responsibilities from application verification and states how to test recovery.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming a managed service removes the need to design queries, permissions or recovery checks.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What evidence would you require before relying on the service’s restore capability?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q020"></a>

### S05-Q020 · Mechanism

<p>How would you choose between one-to-one and one-to-many messaging for a business event or work item?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q020](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q020)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q020](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q020)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare one-to-one and one-to-many messaging patterns.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Identify how many independent recipients must receive the logical information. Distinguish recipient topology from the number of worker replicas.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose message distribution from recipient requirements and consumer ownership.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Compare delivery to one recipient with delivery to several independent recipients; define what “one” means in the proposed design.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Maps a specific business requirement to who must receive each logical message.</li>
<li>Explains how to test distribution when recipients or worker replicas change.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Counting running consumers instead of clarifying which recipients need their own copy.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What changes if a new reporting consumer must receive the same events independently?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q019"></a>

### S05-Q019 · Production decision

<p>How would you make processing reliable when using cloud queues or topics with subscriptions?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q019](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q019)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q019](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q019)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain reliable messaging with queues, topics and subscriptions.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the path from publication to a completed business effect and what happens when a step fails. Reliability here concerns recovery, not just successful message delivery.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design a messaging contract that accounts for interrupted or repeated processing.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify recipient needs, acknowledgment behavior, broker guarantees and failure-recovery ownership; no broker or tier is specified. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces one failed processing attempt and the resulting message and business states.</li>
<li>Defines observable recovery evidence and the boundary of the proposed guarantee.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming a managed broker alone makes the business effect reliable in every failure case.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you verify recovery if a consumer stops immediately after the database commits?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A browser uploads a document for background validation. The application must retain the original file and validation status, and reporting plus notification consumers need the result independently. Propose execution, storage and messaging boundaries; compare an alternative and describe a failed processing attempt. Specify the chosen cloud service and verify its documented limits before relying on them.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Identifies functions, blob storage, relational storage and message distribution with plausible uses.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends one processing path from access, recipient and recovery requirements; states a limit that changes the choice and how to verify it.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Product names or a diagram without data ownership, failure states or a representative verification plan do not establish reliability or cost.</p>
